title: Graphical Representations for One Quantitative Variable
videoTitle: AP Statistics Topic 1.5 Graphical Representations for One Quantitative Variable
intro: Construct and read dotplots, stem-and-leaf plots, and histograms while preserving quantitative order and checking bin boundaries.

moments.title: Quantitative displays
moments.text: The numerical axis preserves the ordering of values.

moments.title: Dotplots
moments.text: Stack observations at their recorded values.

moments.title: Stem-and-leaf plots
moments.text: Split values into ordered stems and leaves, with a key.

moments.title: Bin boundaries
moments.text: The video includes a bin's left endpoint and excludes its right endpoint.

moments.title: Relative frequency histograms
moments.text: Heights may show proportions rather than counts.

moments.title: Lost detail
moments.text: A histogram does not reveal each exact value within a bin.

moments.title: Back-to-back stems
moments.text: Read the shared stem and the leaf key on both sides.

moments.title: Read counts or proportions
moments.text: Check whether the question asks how many or what fraction.

cards.name: Dotplot
cards.text: Use for individual values when stacking dots remains readable.

cards.name: Stem-and-leaf plot
cards.text: Retain digits and include a key that specifies units.

cards.name: Histogram
cards.text: Choose nonoverlapping bins and a frequency or relative frequency scale.

cards.name: Boundary rule
cards.text: Use the stated endpoint convention; changing bins changes the appearance.

questions.q: The tree-height histogram uses intervals 100 up to 150 feet and 150 up to 200 feet, including the left endpoint only. Where does a tree exactly 150 feet tall belong?

work.text: Each bin includes its left endpoint and excludes its right endpoint.

questions.answer: The 150-foot tree belongs in the 150 up to 200 foot bin.

questions.obj: Construct a dotplot from recorded values
questions.q: Supplementary example: delivery times are 12, 14, 14, 18, 21, 23, 27, and 31 minutes. Describe the dotplot.

work.text: Use an equal-interval axis covering 12 through 31 minutes.

steps.t: Place one dot for every observation.

work.text: Place one dot at 12, two stacked dots at 14, and one at each of 18, 21, 23, 27, and 31.
There should be eight dots in total, including both observations at 14.

questions.answer: The dotplot retains the individual times and their repetitions.

traps.title: An empty bin
traps.weak: An empty bin means a missing category label.
traps.better: An empty histogram bin means no observed values fell in that interval.

traps.title: Exact values from bins
traps.weak: Every value in a 10–20 bin equals 15.
traps.better: The bin gives a range, not the individual values.

traps.title: Stems without a key
traps.weak: A leaf 4 after stem 2 must mean 24.
traps.better: Read the key; it might represent 24, 2.4, or another scale.

traps.title: Changing appearance
traps.weak: A different bin width changes the recorded data.
traps.better: It changes the grouping and visible shape, not the observations.

questions.stem: A histogram uses bins [0,5), [5,10), and [10,15). Where is an observation of 10 placed?
why: Each value belongs to exactly one bin.

questions.stem: Which display usually preserves exact recorded values?
opts: A stem-and-leaf plot with a key
A pie chart of grouped intervals
why: The digits and key recover the recorded values.
Relative frequencies do not restore within-bin values.

questions.stem: A histogram has 8, 15, and 7 observations in three bins. What fraction is in the middle bin?
why: 30 is the total, not a proportion.
15 of 30 observations lie in the middle bin.

questions.stem: What can happen when histogram bin widths change?
opts: The apparent number of peaks can change
why: Grouping can reveal or hide peaks.
The recorded data stay the same.

sections.title: Write a complete response
sections.prompt: Eight delivery times, in minutes, are 12, 14, 14, 18, 21, 23, 27, and 31.
parts: (a) Give a stem-and-leaf plot using tens as stems, including a key.
(c) Find the proportion below 20 minutes and explain what detail the histogram loses.
sample: (b) The three bin counts are 4, 3, and 1.
(c) 4/8=0.50, so 50% of deliveries took less than 20 minutes. The histogram does not retain exact times or show that 14 occurs twice.
checklist: Provides a correct key with units.
Finds 50% and explains the loss of exact values.
